title: Water Instead
can_do: 在行动尚未完成前自然地改变选择。
trigger: Mom is about to fill one empty cup with milk when Child realizes he wants water and changes his choice before pouring.
core_response: Actually, can I have water instead?
stretch_response: I changed my mind. Can I have water instead?
essential_props: milk and water pitchers beside one empty transparent cup

turns.speaker: mom
turns.line: Milk or water in your cup?

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: Actually, can I have water instead?

turns.speaker: mom
turns.line: Here's your water. Is that enough?

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: Yes, thank you. That's enough for me.

replay_cards.title: Choose a picnic drink
replay_cards.setting: Packing a drink bottle before going outside
replay_cards.change: Child first picks milk but wants water before Dad fills the still-empty bottle
replay_cards.challenge: Child says, 'I changed my mind. Can I have water instead?' Dad pauses to check which drink he should pack; Child clarifies, 'Water, please, not milk.' Dad confirms the new choice, fills the bottle with water, and puts it in his picnic bag.

replay_cards.title: Switch the bedtime book
replay_cards.change: Change from the train book to the bear book while both books are still available
replay_cards.challenge: Dad opens the train book but has not begun reading. Child asks for the bear book instead. Dad checks the new choice, Child confirms, and they close the train book and begin the bear story.

parent_support: Keep the cup visibly empty while he chooses; pause with the pitcher upright before pouring.
Treat changing his mind as ordinary. Stop the first action, confirm his new choice, and only then pour.
Accept the choice in a warm normal voice. Do not pour milk just to create a reversal, require a reason, or turn the change into a performance of surprise.
